Chapter 9: Preserving Core Values While Stimulating Progress
When an organization reaches a level of true greatness, a new challenge appears—how do you keep that momentum going, year after year? The secret lies in striking a delicate balance. On one hand, you've got to hold tight to the core values that shape who you are. On the other, you need to keep moving forward, adapting and innovating as the world changes around you.
Picture this: your organization is like a mighty tree. The roots run deep—those are your unshakable values and your guiding purpose. They're what give you stability, no matter how rough the weather gets. Meanwhile, the branches stretch out and grow, always reaching for more sunlight. Those branches represent your drive to innovate, your growth, and your ability to adapt. It's all about finding new ways to live out those core values in a world that's always evolving.
The most successful organizations are crystal clear about what can never change. Things like their mission, their values, and the fundamental reason they exist. But when it comes to everything else—strategies, products, processes—they're open to change. They're willing to rethink, reinvent, and realign whenever it's needed to stay competitive and relevant.
So, how can you actually do this in practice? Here are some real-world ways:
First, make sure your core values and purpose are clearly spelled out. Everyone in your organization should know exactly what's non-negotiable.
Next, encourage people to experiment and learn new things—as long as they stay within those core boundaries.
It's also smart to regularly review and update your strategies, systems, and practices. That way, you're always ready for whatever comes next.
And don't forget about leadership. Invest in leaders who can protect what matters most, while also inspiring change and progress.
Think about a company that never wavers in its commitment to customer service. That's a core value. But at the same time, they're always on the lookout for new ways to serve their customers better—maybe it's through new technology, smarter processes, or fresh products.
So, what's the big takeaway here? By finding this balance—honoring your roots while letting your branches grow—you make sure your organization stays true to itself and ready for anything. That's the real secret to lasting greatness.
